comment: The example brand: Kitewell, a made-up kite maker. This one file is everything the engine is told. A setting that is left out takes its default, so most brands need less than this. The skill's rules say what each part means.
name: Kitewell

about.lead: One kite for the whole family. Kitewell flies it in Breeze, and its workshop in Poppy.
about.body: Kitewell is a made-up kite maker. It is here to show what the brand-system skill builds from one drawing, two colours and one typeface.
about.status: An example, not a real brand.
family: Kitewell is the parent. The kite with its lower right facet in Breeze, alone or next to the name.
The workshop is a branch. The same kite with WORKSHOP under the name, and Poppy in place of Breeze.
One accent at a time. Colour says which part of the family is speaking.
Where the name cannot be read, the kite stands alone.

about.lead: Four facets and a tail. The same outline at every size and in every colour version.
facts: The spars are gaps, not lines. The four facets stand apart by one even gap, so the cross is the background showing through.
It leans 21 degrees, the way a kite sits in the wind.

about.lead: The parent. The kite with its lower right facet in Breeze.
The workshop, where kites are built and mended. The same kite, with Poppy in place of Breeze and WORKSHOP under the name.
